Nxeon platform (/opt/nxeon), a VPS/game hosting business. The customer dashboard's "Resource Usage — Across all services" widget (4 donut rings: CPU%, Memory%, Storage%, Network, plus a "30D" toggle) currently shows hardcoded fake literals for every customer regardless of their actual fleet. Confirmed via a prior read-only investigation:

- Data assembled in `/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/page.tsx` around lines 259-267, currently:
```js
// SANDBOX-ONLY. Real in production via lib/proxmox.ts `vmStatus` (cpu, mem,
// maxmem, disk, maxdisk per VM); the sandbox has no hypervisor to ask.
// TODO(prod): fetch client-side after paint — one round-trip per server.
const usage: Usage[] = [
  { label: "CPU", pct: 42, value: "42%", from: "#3fbcd8", to: "#2f7eef" },
  { label: "Memory", pct: 68, value: "68%", from: "#6f37d6", to: "#c026d3" },
  { label: "Storage", pct: 37, value: "37%", from: "#d623e1", to: "#6f2ee0" },
  { label: "Network", pct: 54, value: "2.4 TB", from: "#14c5e4", to: "#11c88e" },
];
```
- Rendered by `components/nx/DashboardView.tsx` (`Donut` components around line 313; the non-functional "30D" toggle button is around lines 315-317, no onClick/state at all).
- Real per-VM telemetry already exists and is used elsewhere in this codebase: `lib/proxmox.ts`'s `vmStatus(vmid)` calls the real Proxmox API and returns real `cpu`, `mem`, `maxmem`, `disk`, `maxdisk` — already used in `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx:266`, `app/admin/servers/[id]/page.tsx:86`, `worker/uptime.ts:35`. Reuse this, don't reinvent it.
- Real bandwidth counters already exist on the `Server` model: `bwInBytes`, `bwOutBytes`, `bwWindowStart` (per earlier DB inspection of a real server row) — check `prisma/schema.prisma` for the exact fields/semantics and how the billing/abuse code (`abuseBwMark`, `bwWindowStart`) already reads them, to reuse the same source of truth rather than inventing a new bandwidth query.

THE TASK — wire this widget up for real:
1. **CPU / Memory / Storage rings**: aggregate REAL usage across all of the logged-in customer's servers (both VPS and game servers, matching however "All Services" is already scoped elsewhere on this same dashboard). Use `vmStatus()` from `lib/proxmox.ts` per server, then combine into one overall percentage per resource — decide a sensible aggregation (e.g. sum(used)/sum(allocated) across all their VMs, weighted by each VM's actual capacity, not a naive average of percentages which would misrepresvent a mix of small/large servers). Handle servers that are stopped/offline (no live stats) or on a node/hypervisor that's unreachable gracefully — don't crash the page, fall back sensibly (e.g. exclude from the live computation, or show a lower-confidence indicator) — and preserve the existing sandbox behavior (this repo runs in an environment with no real Proxmox reachable sometimes — check the existing comment/pattern for how other parts of this codebase already detect "sandbox, no hypervisor" and degrade gracefully, e.g. how `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx` or `worker/uptime.ts` already handle a Proxmox call failing).
2. **Network**: replace the fake "2.4 TB" with the REAL sum of `bwInBytes`+`bwOutBytes` (or whatever the correct real fields/semantics are per schema) across the customer's servers, formatted sensibly (GB/TB as appropriate).
3. **30D toggle**: make it actually functional. Figure out what real windowed data is actually available (check if bandwidth is tracked with enough history to support a real 7-day vs 30-day comparison, or if only a single rolling/current window exists per `bwWindowStart`). If genuine multi-window historical data isn't available without much larger new infrastructure, do NOT fake a toggle that looks functional but isn't — either (a) implement it for real if the data genuinely supports it cheaply, or (b) if it can't be made real without disproportionate new work, replace it with an honest non-interactive label reflecting what's actually being shown (e.g. "Current period" or similar) rather than a fake dropdown/toggle. Use your judgment on which is more in scope, but do not ship another fake interactive control.
4. **Performance**: this runs on every customer's dashboard page load. Live Proxmox API calls per VM can be slow — follow the existing TODO's own suggestion of a client-side fetch after initial paint (so the page shell renders immediately and the usage rings fill in shortly after / show a loading state), rather than blocking full page SSR on N live hypervisor round-trips. Check how other parts of the dashboard already handle this pattern (the "Uptime Average" and "Global Network" stats on this same dashboard were previously wired to real data in commits `6edfa0212a` and `5044b67f66` — look at how those did it for the established convention in this codebase, e.g. an API route + client fetch, and follow the same pattern rather than inventing a new one).
5. Customers with zero servers, or all-offline servers, should see a sensible empty/zero state, not an error or NaN%.

Test in an actual browser (per this repo's established convention — check CLAUDE.md for the dev-server/build-isolation rule, do not run a dev server directly in /opt/nxeon) against a real account with multiple real servers (e.g. nicholas.sj.albanese@gmail.com, which has 5 real servers including some offline ones — good test case for the graceful-degradation path) to confirm the rings show real, sensible numbers and the network figure isn't a random fake value anymore.

Deploy through the normal pipeline: commit -> push -> deploy-staging.sh -> verify HTTP 200 -> promote-production.sh -> verify HTTP 200 AND a genuinely fresh BUILD_ID (compare against the current value, don't trust a stale-looking match).

Report back concisely: what approach you took for each of the 4 metrics and the 30D control, how you verified real numbers render correctly (including the graceful-degradation case), and confirmation of successful production deploy with a fresh BUILD_ID.

**NEVER run `npm run build` in the live prod working tree `/opt/nxeon`.** nxeon-web serves `/opt/nxeon/.next` and nxeon-worker runs `tsx worker/index.ts` off the same tree. A build there overwrites `.next` (new chunk hashes) while the OLD server process keeps running → browser requests chunks by hashes that no longer exist → `ChunkLoadError` / "Something went wrong" on every page (esp. /admin). Also `git checkout <branch>` in the prod tree switches the worker's live code.

**Why:** 2026-08-10 overnight run — I spawned build agents as normal general-purpose agents that `git checkout -b` + `npm run build` INSIDE /opt/nxeon. Each build clobbered prod's compiled assets; prod admin threw ChunkLoadError for hours. Fix was: stop the agent, `git checkout <last-promoted-commit>`, `npm run build`, `chown -R nxeon:nxeon .next`, `systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker`, then hard-refresh the browser.

**How to apply:** build/verify agents MUST work in an ISOLATED git worktree (Agent `isolation: "worktree"`, or manual `git worktree add`) or in `/opt/nxeon-staging` — NEVER the prod tree. The prod tree `/opt/nxeon` should stay parked at the currently-deployed commit; only `scripts/promote-production.sh` (build+restart) moves prod, and only on explicit user authorization. Staging builds go through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` which operates on `/opt/nxeon-staging`. See [[nxeon-ventures-hub]], [[nxeon-platform]].

On the Kodely VM (10.20.0.30), `sudo` commands (nginx config edits, etc.) and `npx prisma db push` against the **prod** database are individually gated by the Claude Code auto-mode permission classifier — this held true even after the user explicitly said "auto run and auto approve everything" earlier in the same conversation (2026-08-17).

On 2026-08-21 I nearly took prod down. In a worktree I created `node_modules` as a symlink to `/opt/nxeon/node_modules` (the standard setup), then ran `git add -A` which COMMITTED the symlink (`.gitignore` has `node_modules/` with a trailing slash, which does NOT match a symlink named `node_modules`). Fast-forwarding that commit into the prod tree `/opt/nxeon` replaced its **real** `node_modules` directory with a **self-referential symlink** (`/opt/nxeon/node_modules -> /opt/nxeon/node_modules`), deleting 1.1G of packages. `next` and the Prisma client became unresolvable; only the in-memory running services survived.

**Why:** never stage the whole tree in a symlinked worktree.
**How to apply:**
- In worktrees, `git add` ONLY the specific files you changed — never `git add -A` / `git add .`.
- Recovery if it happens: `git rm --cached node_modules && rm -f node_modules` in the prod tree, then `npm ci` (lockfile present) + `npx prisma generate`, then commit the untracking. Do this BEFORE any restart/promote — running services hold modules in memory but a build/restart will fail hard.
- Consider hardening `.gitignore` with a bare `node_modules` line (no slash) so the symlink is ignored too.

Relates to [[nxeon-build-isolation]] and the deploy flow in [[nxeon-resume-point]].

# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).

## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session

`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.

1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.

If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).

## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)

- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id). Saved cards live in `PaymentCard` (added with the Nexion schema) — a customer who saved a card before that table existed has their card represented only by the older `User.stripeCustomerId`/`stripePaymentMethodId` columns; `hasChargeableCard`/renewals read those directly and are unaffected, but the Billing page's card list reads `PaymentCard`, so a pre-existing card needs the one-off backfill (`scripts/backfill-payment-cards.ts`) to show up there. That backfill has already been run once for every account with a legacy card as of 2026-09-14; it's idempotent, safe to re-run if a new gap appears.
- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.

## Conventions

- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
- Never fabricate: no invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, or ETAs. If a number can't be read from the database or a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why — this tree has had hash-derived star ratings and fake reviews removed once already.
- Minecraft subdomains (`*.play.nxeon.cloud`) are shared across two tables — `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` and `Server.subdomain` — because both products resolve under the same DNS zone. Always check availability through `lib/game-subdomain.ts`'s `isSubdomainAvailable()` (queries both) rather than checking either table alone, or a free and a paid server can claim the same name.

## Documentation — keep it current (required)

- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. ## Commands

- Typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` (always, before a build)
- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — or, preferably, go through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Working on this codebase" above) so a broken build never lands on a live service.

## Domains & TLS

The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.

/**
 * Bandwidth metering — the one place that decides (a) how Proxmox's per-VM
 * network counters become `Server.bwInBytes` / `bwOutBytes`, and (b) how much
 * confidence a usage figure is allowed to project at the customer.
 *
 * Background: both columns shipped with `@default(0)` and NOTHING ever wrote
 * them. Every plan sells a bandwidth allowance, the billing panel was titled
 * "Transfer used this cycle … versus plan allowance", and it read a permanent
 * `0 B / 20 TB · 0%`. Downstream, `worker/abuse.ts` computed its outbound rate
 * from `bwOutBytes` deltas, so `deltaBytes` was always 0 and BANDWIDTH_SPIKE
 * could never fire: the platform shipped an abuse detector that could not
 * detect anything. This module is the missing signal.
 *
 * Two hard rules, both of which exist because a *confidently wrong* number is
 * worse here than a visibly incomplete one:
 *
 *  1. Never invent traffic. Proxmox `netin`/`netout` are cumulative per QEMU
 *     PROCESS, not per VM lifetime — a stop/start, a hard reset, a reinstall or
 *     a live migration replaces the process and the counters restart at 0. A
 *     naive `cur - prev` then goes hugely negative, and (when the fresh boot has
 *     already pushed more than the stale baseline held) it can just as easily go
 *     hugely positive. Either way the delta is fiction, and fiction that feeds
 *     an abuse detector can suspend a paying customer. `creditFromCounters`
 *     detects the restart and credits only bytes it can prove happened inside
 *     the interval.
 *  2. Never present a partial period as authoritative. The meter can only know
 *     traffic from the moment it started sampling. `bwUsageView` reports the
 *     period it actually covers, and refuses to render a percentage at all when
 *     no sample has ever been taken — a "0 B / 20 TB · 0%" that means "we never
 *     looked" is exactly the defect class this codebase keeps repeating.
 *
 * Plain module (no "use server"): imported by the worker sweep
 * (worker/monitor.ts), by worker/abuse.ts and by the customer billing page.
 */

import { getSetting, setSetting } from "./settings";

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Metering-run markers
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// These live in the `Setting` KV rather than on Server rows because
// prisma/schema.prisma is frozen — and because they are genuinely global: one
// sweep meters every VM at once. They are what lets the UI say "measured since"
// and "last updated" instead of implying the number is complete.

/** First sweep that successfully sampled at least one VM. Null = never metered. */
export const BW_STARTED_AT_KEY = "bw_meter_started_at";
/**
 * END of the most recent sweep that sampled at least one VM.
 *
 * The end, not the start, and that matters: this timestamp is where an RRD
 * back-fill after a worker restart begins counting. Anchored to the sweep start
 * it would re-count the traffic of every server the previous sweep sampled after
 * that instant — inventing traffic, which is the one thing metering must never
 * do. Anchored to the end it can only ever lose a few seconds.
 */
export const BW_LAST_AT_KEY = "bw_meter_last_at";
/** Last time the meter was down longer than it can back-fill (traffic was lost). */
export const BW_GAP_AT_KEY = "bw_meter_gap_at";
/**
 * Last time the meter back-filled a restart gap from RRD. Back-filled bytes land
 * in one write but describe up to an hour of traffic, so any rate computed over
 * that window is inflated. worker/abuse.ts reads this and sits out the affected
 * window rather than raising a spike alert on an accounting artefact.

## No game container had a log-size cap — one crash-loop filled a customer's disk to 100% (2026-09-17)

**Live incident**: `projectzomboid-kc0kcr` (VM 121) crash-looped for an extended period (systemd
`NRestarts` on its generated unit had reached 10,148) because its root disk filled completely and every
subsequent start attempt failed with `OCI runtime exec failed: ... no space left on device`. Breakdown of
the 77 GB root disk at 100%: **~28 GB** was Docker's `json-file` log for the game container — no image's
setup script has ever set `--log-opt max-size`/`max-file`, so a container restarting every few seconds
forever grows that log without bound; **~28.5 GB** was `/var/log/syslog` + `.1`, pure rsyslog spam from
logging its own "no space left on device" write failures once the disk was already full (a feedback loop,
not a separate cause); the remaining **~11 GB** was the customer's real game data (binaries/mods/save),
correctly sized and untouched.

**Live remediation** (this customer only, read-only-diagnosis-plus-truncate, no credentials touched): SSH'd
in via the platform's own `withServerSsh`/`exec` (`lib/ssh-exec.ts`, same connection path the control panel
itself uses), confirmed the exact log path with `docker inspect --format '{{.LogPath}}' <id>`, then
`truncate -s 0` (never `rm`, so Docker's and rsyslog's open file handles stayed valid) on that path and on
`/var/log/syslog`/`syslog.1`. `df -h /` went from 77G/100% used/0 avail to 22G used / 56G avail (29%).
Systemd's own `Restart=always` (see `wrapDockerGameService` below) then recovered the container on its
own once space existed — confirmed `docker ps` healthy, `NRestarts` stopped climbing, game logs showing a
real startup (workshop mod validation → world load → "Initialising Server Systems") rather than an
immediate re-crash, and the game's UDP/TCP ports actually listening. `Server.status` in the DB already
read `RUNNING` throughout and needed no correction.

**Systemic fix, for every future game provision**: `wrapDockerGameService()` in `worker/index.ts` is the
one shared point every game family's per-image `docker run -d --name X ...` setup script (defined
independently per family across `prisma/seed-wave*-games.ts`) gets rewritten through, into `docker create`
plus a generated systemd unit — see the existing 2026-08-26 entry above for why that rewrite exists at
all. It now also injects `--log-opt max-size=10m --log-opt max-file=3` (a 30 MB ceiling per container,
regardless of family or how long/hard it crash-loops) into that same rewritten `docker create` invocation,
so this is fixed once for all ~40+ game families rather than needing a per-family edit. Deliberately
forward-only: the already-running `projectzomboid` container above was NOT re-created to pick up the cap
(doing so would mean touching another customer's live container beyond the disk-space fix it needed) — it
applies starting with the next order of any game.

## Deploy wizard plan cards now headline the intro price, not the renewal price (2026-09-17)

**What changed.** The VPS and game-server deploy wizards (both served by the single Nexion
`components/nx/DeployView.tsx`, plan cards in `components/nx/OrderBits.tsx`'s `PlanCard`, game tier
cards inline in `DeployView.tsx`'s "Size your server" step) used to show the **regular/renewal**
price as the big headline number, with a small amber "$X/mo first term, then $Y/mo" line underneath
for any plan/tier carrying an admin-set intro rate (`Plan.introPriceCents`/`GamePlan.introPriceCents`
— see `lib/intro-pricing.ts`). That is now inverted, matching the standard hosting-industry pattern
(DigitalOcean, Hostinger, etc.):

- The card's headline is now the **intro price** when one is set (the smallest real price a new
  customer pays) — `PlanCard`'s `headlineCents` and the equivalent local in the game tier card.
- The "then $Y/mo" renewal figure no longer lives on the card. It moved to the **Order summary**
  step (`DeployView.tsx`, right below "Left to pay"), worded "Renews at $Y/mo after your first
  month." on a Monthly-term order or "...after your first term." on Annual/2yr/3yr — never
  hardcoded "month" for a longer term, since a longer term's intro discount covers the *whole*
  first term, not one month of it (`o.termMonths === 1` gate).
- Cards with an intro rate now carry a real, server-computed "🔥 X% off first month/term — limited
  time" badge. `X` is `introBadgePercent()` (`app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx`) —

## Dashboard "Resource Usage" widget is now real, not hardcoded literals (2026-09-17)

**What was wrong.** The customer dashboard's "Resource Usage — Across all services" card (four donut
rings: CPU/Memory/Storage/Network, plus a "30D" pill) rendered the exact same four numbers —
`42% / 68% / 37% / 2.4 TB` — for every customer regardless of their real fleet. The "30D" control was a
plain `<button>` with no `onClick`, no state, nothing behind it. Both had been marked `SANDBOX-ONLY` /
`TODO(prod)` in `app/dashboard/page.tsx` since the Nexion port, because the real source
(`lib/proxmox.ts`'s `vmStatus`) needs one live hypervisor round trip per provisioned VM — too slow to
`await` in this page's server component without delaying the whole dashboard's first paint.

**What changed.** New route `GET /api/dashboard/resource-usage` computes real, capacity-weighted totals
across the customer's VPS + game-server rows (the same `db.server` scope this dashboard's own service
table already uses — Shared Hosting / free Minecraft carry neither Proxmox VM stats nor these bandwidth
counters, so they stay out of this widget exactly like they already do out of its "All Services" filter
tabs):
- **CPU** — one live `vmStatus()` per provisioned VM (`Promise.allSettled`, `pveForNode(server.node)`
  when set, matching `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx`'s own per-node-connection pattern). Combined as
  `sum(cpuFraction × cores) / sum(cores)` — weighted by each VM's real vCPU count, not a naive average of
  percentages, so one maxed 1-vCPU box and one idle 8-vCPU box don't average to "50%". A STOPPED VM
  answers this call fine with real zeroed cpu/mem and its real `maxmem` — that's genuine live data (0%
  used is true when it's off), so it's included exactly like a RUNNING one. Only an actual failure (vmid
  missing on the hypervisor — e.g. a staging/sandbox row — or the node unreachable) drops a server from
  the sum, silently, same "an API error is our blind spot" rule `worker/uptime.ts` already follows.
- **Memory** — `sum(mem) / sum(maxmem)` from the same live call, no second round trip.
- **Storage** — deliberately NOT a live guest-agent call. Confirmed against this box's own
  `/cluster/resources`: Proxmox reports `disk: 0` for every QEMU VM regardless of real usage (the
  hypervisor can't see inside the guest), so the only real number is the QEMU-guest-agent `get-fsinfo`
  reading — and the worker already samples that into `ServerDiskSample` every ~10 minutes
  (`worker/monitor.ts`'s `sampleServerDisks`, existing infra powering the per-server disk chart). This
  route reads the latest stored sample per server instead of stacking a second live call on top of the
  CPU/Memory one.
- **Network** — the exact same `bwInBytes`/`bwOutBytes`/`bwWindowStart` counters and `bwUsageView()` /
  `readBwMeterHealth()` (`lib/bandwidth.ts`) the Billing page's Bandwidth card already reads — one source
  of truth, not a second formula. Summed across servers into one used-bytes figure and one percent of
  total allowance.
- **Zero/empty state** — a customer with no servers, or every server excluded (no live signal at all),
  reads `measured: false` for that metric: the ring shows `—`, never a fabricated `0%`.

**The "30D" control.** `lib/bandwidth.ts`'s meter is a single rolling 30-day window
(`BW_PERIOD_DAYS = 30`) — there is no second stored period (no 7-day archive) to switch to, so a
functional toggle would need materially new metering infrastructure. Per the "don't ship a fake
interactive control" call, it's now a plain non-interactive `<span>` (`cursor-default`, no hover state,
no chip styling that implies clickability) reading "Last 30 days" (or "Since <date>" while the window is
still filling for a newly-metered server, or "Not measured yet" if nothing has been metered at all) —
honest about what's actually being shown instead of a dropdown-styled button that did nothing.

new client component, `components/nx/ResourceUsageCard.tsx`, which fetches the route above in a

with real numbers moments later. `app/dashboard/page.tsx` no longer computes or passes a `usage` prop at
all — `DashboardView`'s `Usage` type and prop were removed since the card is now fully self-contained.

#!/bin/bash
# Promote the currently deployed staging commit to production.
# Verifies staging is healthy, fast-forwards nothing (prod working tree IS the repo),
# then rebuilds + restarts production services.
set -euo pipefail

STG_COMMIT=$(git -C /opt/nxeon-staging rev-parse HEAD)
PROD_COMMIT=$(git -C /opt/nxeon rev-parse HEAD)

echo "==> Staging is at:    $STG_COMMIT"
echo "==> Production is at: $PROD_COMMIT"

if ! systemctl is-active -q nxeon-staging-web; then
  echo "Refusing to promote: staging web service is not running." >&2
  exit 1
fi
CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8080/)
if [ "$CODE" != "200" ]; then
  echo "Refusing to promote: staging returns HTTP $CODE." >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [ "$STG_COMMIT" != "$PROD_COMMIT" ]; then
  echo "Note: production tree is at a different commit than staging."
  echo "Production deploys directly from /opt/nxeon's working tree (main)."
fi

cd /opt/nxeon
echo "==> Installing dependencies (adds any new deps before build)"
# CRITICAL: without this, a commit that adds a new dependency (e.g. imapflow)
# builds against a stale node_modules and fails — which previously aborted the
# promote AFTER the old build was already gone. Always sync deps first.
npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -3
# CRITICAL: this was previously `prisma generate` only — regenerates the
# CLIENT's types (fixes the build) but never touches the actual DATABASE.
# Staging and production are SEPARATE databases (nxeon_staging vs nxeon, same
# Postgres server, confirmed live) — deploy-staging.sh's own `db push` only
# ever applies to staging's DB, so a schema change promoted this way built
# and deployed fine while production's actual table never got the new
# column, silently breaking the FIRST thing that queried it post-deploy
# (found live 2026-09-02: worker/billing.ts's sweeps started throwing
# "column does not exist" immediately after a routine promote — no staging
# failure gave any warning, since staging's own db push had already
# succeeded there). `db push` both applies the schema AND regenerates the
# client, so this replaces the old generate-only step rather than adding a
# second one. Schema changes are rare enough that this always running
# unconditionally costs nothing when there's nothing new to push.
echo "==> Applying database schema"
npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss --schema=/opt/nxeon/prisma/schema.prisma 2>&1 | tail -4
echo "==> Building production"
npm run build 2>&1 | tail -4
# Guard: never restart into an incomplete/failed build. A valid production build
# always writes .next/BUILD_ID; if it's missing the build failed mid-way and the
# old in-memory process is still serving — abort rather than kill it.
if [ ! -s /opt/nxeon/.next/BUILD_ID ]; then
  echo "BUILD FAILED: .next/BUILD_ID missing — NOT restarting (old process left serving)." >&2
  exit 1
fi
# next.config sets output:"standalone"; the standalone server.js is what the
# systemd unit actually runs (not `next start` — see deploy-staging.sh's own
# comment on this same step for the 2026-09-10 incident). Its output does NOT
# include public/ or .next/static/ (Next's documented behavior) — refresh
# them every promote, same as staging, or new/changed static assets are
# missing from prod until the next promote happens to also touch this step.
echo "==> Copying static assets into the standalone server output"
rm -rf .next/standalone/public .next/standalone/.next/static
cp -r public .next/standalone/public
cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/static
# geoip-lite is in next.config.ts's serverExternalPackages (kept OUT of the JS
# bundle since it reads .dat files off its own package path at runtime) — the
# standalone output tracer only copies files it can trace as JS-imported, so
# an externalized package's own non-JS data files are silently left behind.
# Found live 2026-09-10 on staging: this crashes EVERY request with an
# uncaught ENOENT the moment something runs the standalone server.js instead
# of `next start` — geo-ip.ts's own try/catch around geoip.lookup() does NOT
# help, the failure isn't confined to that call. Copy the real data/
# directory every promote, same reasoning as public/.next/static above. This
# has NOT yet bitten production because nxeon-web's systemd unit still runs
# `npm start` (next start) today, not server.js directly — but this fix must
# land before that switch happens, not after.
if [ -d node_modules/geoip-lite/data ]; then
  mkdir -p .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data
  cp -r node_modules/geoip-lite/data/. .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data/
fi
# Web runs as the unprivileged 'nxeon' user. .next needs to be writable by it
# (Next cache); the rest stays root-owned and world-readable. .env is the one
# exception: systemd's EnvironmentFile= reads it as root (PID 1, pre-privilege
# drop) so the app's process env is fine either way, but Prisma's generated
# client ALSO opens .env directly at Client instantiation to resolve its own
# env() directives — that read happens as the actual 'nxeon' process user, so
# a root-owned .env throws EACCES there on every cold start (harmless once
# systemd's injected vars are already in process.env, but noisy, and a prior
# root-run edit to this file silently reverted the ownership fix below once
# already — confirmed live 2026-09-02). Keep .env nxeon-owned, not world- or
# group-readable. Do NOT chown the whole tree (breaks root git on .git).
echo "==> Fixing .next/.env ownership for non-root web"
chown -R nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon/.next 2>/dev/null || true
chown nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon/.env 2>/dev/null || true
chmod 600 /opt/nxeon/.env 2>/dev/null || true
echo "==> Restarting production web"
systemctl restart nxeon-web

# Drain in-flight provisions before bouncing the worker. Restarting the worker
# mid-provision used to interrupt a live VM build and (with a non-idempotent retry)
# strand the server in ERROR. The start step is now idempotent so this is
# belt-and-suspenders, but avoiding the interruption entirely is cleaner. Bounded
# wait (max ~4 min) so a deploy can never hang forever.
DBURL=$(grep -E '^DATABASE_URL=' /opt/nxeon/.env | head -1 | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '"')
if [ -n "$DBURL" ] && command -v psql >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  for _ in $(seq 1 24); do
    ACTIVE=$(psql "$DBURL" -tAc "SELECT count(*) FROM \"Job\" WHERE status='RUNNING' AND type='PROVISION';" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')
    [ "${ACTIVE:-0}" = "0" ] && break
    echo "==> Waiting for ${ACTIVE} in-flight provision(s) to finish before restarting worker…"
    sleep 10
  done
fi

echo "==> Restarting production worker"
systemctl restart nxeon-worker
sleep 5
systemctl is-active nxeon-web nxeon-worker
CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1/)
echo "==> Production responds: HTTP $CODE"
[ "$CODE" = "200" ] || { echo "PRODUCTION UNHEALTHY — check journalctl -u nxeon-web"; exit 1; }
echo "==> Production promote complete"

content.text:
The dashboard's Resource Usage widget is now wired to real per-customer data. Here's the summary:

**Approach per metric** (new route `app/api/dashboard/resource-usage/route.ts`, fetched client-side by new `components/nx/ResourceUsageCard.tsx` after mount — same pattern as the existing `NetworkStatusModal`/`/api/dashboard/network-status`):

- **CPU**: one live `vmStatus()` per provisioned VM (`Promise.allSettled`, per-node connection via `pveForNode`, matching `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx`'s established pattern). Combined as `sum(cpuFraction × cores) / sum(cores)` — capacity-weighted, not a naive average. A stopped VM answers the call fine with real zeroed stats, so it's included as genuine 0%; only an actual failure (vmid missing on the hypervisor, node unreachable) drops a server from the sum, same rule `worker/uptime.ts` already follows.
- **Memory**: `sum(mem) / sum(maxmem)` from that same live call, no extra round trip.
- **Storage**: deliberately *not* a live guest-agent call. Confirmed live against this box's own `/cluster/resources` that Proxmox reports `disk: 0` for every QEMU VM — so it reads the latest `ServerDiskSample` row per server instead (the worker already samples this every ~10 min for the existing disk chart), avoiding a second per-VM round trip.
- **Network**: reuses `bwInBytes`/`bwOutBytes`/`bwUsageView()`/`readBwMeterHealth()` from `lib/bandwidth.ts` — the same source the Billing page's bandwidth card already reads, not a second formula.
- **Zero/empty state**: any metric with no live signal returns `measured:false` → ring shows `—`, never a fabricated `0%`.

**30D control**: `lib/bandwidth.ts`'s meter is a single rolling 30-day window with no second stored period — a functional toggle isn't cheaply real. Replaced the dead `<button>` with a non-interactive `<span>` (`cursor-default`, no hover/chip styling) reading "Last 30 days" / "Since <date>" / "Not measured yet".

**Verification performed**: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean throughout. Deployed via `deploy-staging.sh` (HTTP 200). On staging, confirmed via both a real Playwright browser session and a direct curl of the authenticated SSR HTML that a fresh zero-server account renders the honest empty state end-to-end ("—" rings, "Not measured yet" pill, no `500`/`NaN`, none of the old `42%`/`68%`/`37%`/`2.4 TB` literals anywhere). The route returns clean `401` unauthenticated and clean `200` authenticated. **One gap**: I could not verify the real multi-server/offline-server account (`nicholas.sj.albanese@gmail.com`) — the harness's own permission gate refused admin impersonation of that specific named customer's live account, and I did not attempt to route around it. That path is covered by code review (it reuses the exact `Promise.allSettled` degradation pattern already proven live in `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx` and `worker/uptime.ts`) but not by an observed live number — flagged honestly in the docs entry and worth a follow-up check by whoever has interactive admin access.

**Deploy**: committed (`bc2a67626b`, plus a follow-up docs correction `30e4e150f0`) and auto-pushed. Production is confirmed serving this code: another concurrent session promoted `main` (which has my commit as an ancestor) to production during this work — verified via `git log` ancestry, `BUILD_ID wbG5LO9Yotu1gGdpxKdY8` (built minutes prior), HTTP 200 on `/`, and the new route correctly returning 401 unauthenticated on prod.
